page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with marginal notes in the left margin (short notes beside lines 3 and 22). The right margin holds a column of printed notes, cut off by the scan edge. Running head "Epistola" at the top centre. No page number, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: PlantaQuid auro ductilius? Quid argento nitidius? Quid ferro solidius? Quid plumbo liquabilius? Quid Mercurio mobilius? De plantis quid dicam. Quam divite & admiranda in ijs varietate ludat Natura, eloqui mortale os vix potest. Nec enim repertum credo, qui omnes plantarum differentias, nedum virtutes vel fando exploratas habuerit, etsi in explorandis ijs nihil reliquum humana fecit industria. In cœlum nonnullæ assurgunt, fixis ad centrum radicibus, supra humum aliæ non attolluntur: amant aliæ montes, aliæ convalles, aliæ planities, aliæ vmbrosa, aliæ aprica, aliæ sicca, aliæ humida, aliæ calida, aliæ frigida loca, aliæ saxa, glebas aliæ. Temperamentorum, colorum, figurarum, & virtutum taceo varietatem admirandam. Memorat Plinius, lib. 22. cap. 3. in majestate populi terrarum principis, præmiisque gloriæ, graminea corona nullam fuisse nobiliorem: gemmatas, aureas post hanc fuisse, & ab vniverso exercitu servato non nisi Imperatori datam. page.notes: Left margin: "Planta" beside the line "plantis quid dicam". Left margin, beside "tatem admirandam": a handwritten or small printed note "gramen aureo ... praelatum ... Romani", partly illegible; the readings are doubtful. The right margin is cut off by the scan edge; its roughly 18 short lines of note text are not legible enough to transcribe and are left out. The last word of the page is "seni-", hyphenated, with its continuation on the next page. Printed spelling kept as is (ductilius, nitidius, assurgunt, fœtibus).
